elevated content card; distinguished by fill lightness not border
the one CTA; matches icon+backdrop; brand accent NOT system accent

patterns.key_values: single elevated content card #2A2A2E on #1A1E20 window, ~12pt radius, centred icon->name->status-pill stack, equal L/R inset shared with the CTA
onboarding-flavoured single-view: centred app-name title + 1-line secondary subtitle + one concrete example card + exactly one full-width primary CTA; one-decision surface
status pill: capsule, macOS system green #30D158 fill, dark text, leading checkmark glyph = confirmed/installed state (colour always paired with glyph)

signature_moves: Brand owns the actions, OS owns the meanings: CTA in brand teal #23B7A5, status state in macOS system green #30D158 with a checkmark glyph
Tinted dark ground (#1A1E20 cool/teal) instead of neutral #1E1E1E, so the surface reads as brand-owned with no accent pixel in the chrome
One-decision surface: centred name + single concrete example card + one CTA (Hick's Law at its floor)
defects: Contrast Dilution (mild) — subtitle #7F8086 on #1A1E20 approx 4.3:1, under AA 4.5:1
Non-native CTA idiom — full-width filled button + outer glow (web/iOS pattern) instead of a standard macOS push button; systematic/purposeful so a tell not a hard defect
Brand accent over system accent — primary binds to teal not the user's system accent (deviation, acceptable house style for a branded consumer utility)

aesthetic.direction: Neo-grotesque product (dark neutral ramp + one electric accent) applied to a native Mac micro-utility; marketing layer adds a grotesk-vs-serif-italic display pairing
peers: CleanShot X / Setapp-class single-purpose Mac utilities

psychology: Von Restorff / signal detection — the lone saturated teal CTA breaks a dark field, so the one action is instantly found
Jakob's Law — familiar Mac window frame + system green for 'installed' meets trained user expectations for a Mac utility
Peak-End / Doherty feedback — the green 'Installed in Safari' confirmation makes the success moment visible, closing the loop
Hick's Law — a one-decision surface with zero choice overload, correct for a single-task converter
Demonstrate don't describe — the card shows a real extension (Dark Reader icon + real install state) rather than abstract copy
